bugs: No functional bugs found. Probes passed: a real database worker retried 3 times, then wrote a failed_jobs row and set crm_last_error; a stale claim was re-dispatched after 16 min; a job for a deleted model was discarded.

Efficiency issue, not a bug: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:22 runs lazyById over every unsynced subscriber, including ones already in flight, and issues a claim UPDATE for each one every minute. During a queue backlog, which is exactly the problem scenario, that becomes N no-op write queries per minute.
antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:22 – the outer query does not filter on crm_sync_queued_at, so the per-row claim UPDATE runs even for rows it will skip.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:64-71 – asserts config by reflecting on the Tries/Backoff attributes instead of on behaviour. This is brittle and couples the test to implementation details.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:11 – a public const CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES exists mainly so a test can read it. A config value would fit the app better.
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, re-dispatching rows that are already in flight, withoutOverlapping's default 24h lock expiry, and chunk() paginating over a column it mutates. Fixes them with minimal diffs.

Uses modern queue attributes (Tries, MaxExceptions, Backoff, DeleteWhenMissingModels), checked against vendor. Sets tries above max exceptions so WithoutOverlapping releases do not use up the retries.
The job has an idempotency guard (skips if already synced) and a failed() hook that records crm_last_error.
Uses an atomic conditional UPDATE to claim each row, so concurrent dispatchers cannot both queue the same subscriber.
Has a test that queues more subscribers than one lazyById chunk.

app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:12-13 – switches to the #[Signature]/#[Description] attributes in one command only, while NormalizeSubscriberEmails keeps the properties. The style is inconsistent.
strengths: Same correct root-cause fixes as impl-1: rethrow plus failed(), claim-based dispatch with stale requeue, withoutOverlapping(5), and chunkById.
The outer query already excludes rows that are in flight, so a backed-up queue does not trigger per-row UPDATEs every minute.
Moves the requeue TTL into config/services.php instead of hard-coding it as a constant.
Adds Timeout(30), which is consistent with the 10s HTTP timeout and the 120s overlap-lock expiry.
The tests include a dispatch through the sync queue that exercises failed() end to end, and the assertions are behavioural rather than reflection-based.

v.rationale:
The two implementations are nearly the same. Each fixes all four root causes:
1. The try/catch swallowed the exception, so the job never retried or failed. Both now rethrow and add failed() and attribute-based retries/backoff.
2. Every minute the dispatcher re-queued subscribers that were already queued. Both now claim rows atomically on crm_sync_queued_at with a stale TTL, and the job skips subscribers that are already synced.
3. Scheduler withoutOverlapping() defaults to a 24h lock expiry. Both shorten it.
4. chunk() paginated over the email_normalized column it was updating. Both switch to chunkById.

Both suites pass (14 tests each). The same three probes passed on both: a real database worker retried and then wrote failed_jobs, a stale claim was requeued, and a job for a missing model was discarded.

impl-2 ranks first because its dispatcher filters out in-flight rows in the outer query, so a backed-up queue does not cause N no-op UPDATEs per minute. It also puts the TTL in config, and its tests check behaviour, including failed() through the sync queue, rather than reflecting on attributes. Its weaknesses are a duplicated where closure, inconsistent use of the command attributes, and a test name that overclaims. impl-1's 1100-row chunk-boundary test is a nice addition, but it does not make up for the extra per-row writes and the brittle reflection test.
